tagline_zh: 甘甜溪水做的手工豆腐小街
tagline_en: A tofu lane built on sweet mountain spring water
story_zh: 洗水坑位於洗水溪與汶水溪匯流處，是客家人與泰雅族混居的地帶，前往泰安溫泉的苗62線一定會經過。當地以甘甜水質與古法手工製作豆腐聞名，丁字型的石板小街兩側有客家舊屋與豆腐店，臭豆腐、豆花與豆腐乳都是招牌。這是因美食而興起的「老街」，老建築有限，假日遊客多。
story_en: Xishuikeng lies where the Xishui and Wenshui streams meet, a mixed Hakka and Atayal area on the road to Tai'an hot springs. It is famous for handmade tofu said to owe its taste to the sweet local water, and a small T-shaped stone-paved lane is lined with tofu shops and old Hakka houses. It is more food stop than historic street, and busy on weekends.
getting_there: 建議開車
best_time: 泡完泰安溫泉順遊；假日停車較難

tagline_zh: 全台最大木雕聚落的藝品街
tagline_en: Woodcarving galleries in Taiwan's carving capital
story_zh: 三義因清代樟腦業興盛，砍伐樟樹後剩下的樹頭被加工成木雕，木雕業接棒成為主要產業，今為全台最大的木雕聚落。今日遊客所說的三義老街多指水美一帶的木雕街，兩側木雕藝品店林立，屬戰後興起的商業街而非歷史老街。可搭配1995年開館的三義木雕博物館一起參觀。
story_en: Sanyi grew rich on camphor in the Qing era, and when the camphor trees were felled their leftover stumps were carved, so woodcarving took over as the local industry; it is now Taiwan's largest carving community. What visitors call Sanyi Old Street is usually the Shuimei woodcarving street, lined with galleries and shops—a postwar commercial street rather than a historic one. Pair it with the Sanyi Wood Sculpture Museum, opened in 1995.
getting_there: 台鐵三義站轉乘或開車約5分鐘
best_time: 4–5月桐花季

tagline_zh: 三義地名由來的「三叉河」舊街仔
tagline_en: The original 'Sanchahe' street that gave Sanyi its name
story_zh: 廣盛老街是三義聚落的發源地，在地人稱「舊街仔」，原名「三叉河」，因附近溪流在此交匯；官方嫌「叉」字不雅，改為形近的「义」，即今日的三義。清代樟腦交易讓此地成為市街，後由木雕業接續。老街建築大多已改建為一般樓房，鄉公所近年以牆面彩繪打造「好客走廊」。
story_en: Guangsheng is where Sanyi began; locals call it the 'old street', and its original name Sanchahe ('three-forked river') came from streams meeting here. Officials disliked the character for 'fork' and swapped it for the similar-looking 'yi', giving today's Sanyi. Camphor trade made it a market town, later succeeded by woodcarving; most buildings have been rebuilt, and the township has added murals along a 'Hakka hospitality corridor'.
getting_there: 台鐵三義站步行約5分鐘

tagline_zh: 白沙屯媽祖徒步進香的起點廟前街
tagline_en: The temple street where the Baishatun Mazu pilgrimage begins
story_zh: 白沙屯老街俗稱店仔街，就在拱天宮廟前，狹小巷弄是參拜與逛街的主要動線。拱天宮的白沙屯媽祖每年徒步往北港進香，路線不固定、由神轎決定，已有近200年歷史，近年參與者動輒數十萬人。平時老街安靜，進香出發與回鑾期間則人潮洶湧。
story_en: Baishatun Old Street, locally called Dianzai Street, is the narrow lane in front of Gongtian Temple. The temple's Mazu makes an annual walking pilgrimage to Beigang whose route is decided by the palanquin itself, a tradition of nearly 200 years that now draws hundreds of thousands of followers. Quiet most of the year, the street overflows during the pilgrimage's departure and return.
getting_there: 台鐵白沙屯站步行約15分鐘
best_time: 農曆年後至春季媽祖進香期間最熱鬧，但交通壅塞

tagline_zh: 水果之鄉的舊市街
tagline_en: The old market quarter of a fruit-growing town
story_zh: 卓蘭是大安溪畔的客家水果之鄉，舊市街位於中街里一帶。1956年開幕的大光明戲院曾見證小鎮的熱鬧，約於1970年代歇業。關於老街本身的文史與觀光資料相當稀少，現況多為一般住宅與商店。
story_en: Zhuolan is a Hakka fruit-growing town on the Da'an River, with its old market quarter in Zhongjie village. The Daguangming Theatre, opened in 1956, recalls busier days and is believed to have closed around the 1970s. Little has been written about the old street itself, which is now mostly ordinary homes and shops.
getting_there: 建議開車
best_time: 水果產季（葡萄、楊桃）可順遊

address_hint: 中正路、復興路、平陽路一帶（福興村）
tagline_zh: 杭菊之鄉的樸實客家舊街
tagline_en: A plain Hakka main street in chrysanthemum country
story_zh: 銅鑼清代墾號名為「福興」，老街原址至今仍屬福興村，是市街的發源地。1935年中部大地震重創老街，此後逐漸沒落，如今是樸實的一般社區。可在周邊品嘗水粄、發粿等客家米食，秋冬順遊杭菊花田與臺灣客家文化館。
story_en: Tongluo's Qing-era name was Fuxing, and the old street, still in Fuxing village, is where the town began. The 1935 earthquake badly damaged it and it slowly declined into an ordinary residential area. Come for Hakka rice cakes nearby and, in late autumn, the chrysanthemum fields and the Taiwan Hakka Museum.
getting_there: 台鐵銅鑼站步行約5分鐘
best_time: 11–12月杭菊花季

tagline_zh: 舊山線最高點車站前的木屋小吃街
tagline_en: Wooden snack street at the old mountain line's highest station
story_zh: 勝興車站舊名十六份驛，建於日治時期，是舊山線海拔最高的車站，1998年舊山線停駛後成為熱門懷舊景點。車站前保留一整排木造老屋，如今是賣擂茶、麻糬與客家菜的小吃街。舊山線鐵道自行車營運後人潮更多，可延伸至龍騰斷橋。
story_en: Shengxing Station, originally Jurokufun, was built in the Japanese era as the highest station on the old mountain railway line, and became a nostalgia hotspot after the line closed in 1998. The row of wooden houses in front of it is now a snack street selling lei cha, mochi and Hakka dishes. The old-line rail bikes have made it even busier, and it links to the Longteng broken bridge.
getting_there: 建議開車；或台鐵三義站轉乘計程車/台灣好行
best_time: 假日人多；鐵道自行車需提早訂票

address_hint: 中山路（台中車站至第二市場一帶）
tagline_zh: 日治「鈴蘭通」，台中舊城最熱鬧的一條街
tagline_en: Taichung's Japanese-era 'Lily-of-the-valley Street', the old downtown's main drag
story_zh: 中山路在日治大正年間稱為「新盛橋通」，因綠川上的新盛橋得名，街燈做成鈴蘭花造型，又有「鈴蘭通」的美稱，是當年台中最繁華的商業街。戰後市中心西移、舊城一度沒落，直到宮原眼科等日治老建築被活化成伴手禮店爆紅，才把人潮重新帶回這一帶。街尾的第二市場以六角樓為中心，至今仍是在地人吃早午餐的美食據點。
story_en: In the Taishō era this stretch of Zhongshan Road was named Shinseibashi-dori after the bridge over the Lüchuan canal, and its lily-of-the-valley street lamps earned it the nickname 'Suzuran-dori'. It was Taichung's smartest shopping street until the city centre drifted west after the war. The revival of colonial buildings such as the Miyahara eye clinic, now a famous sweets shop, brought crowds back, while the hexagonal Second Market at the far end remains a local breakfast institution.
getting_there: 台中車站出站步行約3分鐘即達
best_time: 平日上午人較少；第二市場以早午餐時段最熱鬧

tagline_zh: 旱溪媽祖廟前的舊聚落，老屋多已改建
tagline_en: Old settlement around the Hanxi Mazu temple; most old houses are gone
story_zh: 旱溪街一帶以清乾隆年間創建的樂成宮（旱溪媽祖廟）為核心發展，廟方每年農曆三月的「旱溪媽祖遶境大屯十八庄」已有近兩百年歷史。街區的舊建築多已改建為現代樓房，老街風貌所剩無幾，如今主要吸引香客與附近夜市人潮。
story_en: The Hanxi area grew up around Lecheng Temple, a Mazu temple founded in the Qianlong era of the Qing dynasty, whose annual pilgrimage through the 'eighteen villages of Datun' has run for nearly two centuries. Almost all the old shophouses have been rebuilt, so today the draw is the temple and the snacks around it rather than the streetscape.
getting_there: 台中車站搭公車至樂成宮站，或自台中車站騎車約10分鐘
best_time: 農曆三月旱溪媽祖遶境期間最熱鬧

address_hint: 順天路、蔣公路一帶（鎮瀾宮周邊）
tagline_zh: 跟著媽祖吃糕餅，大甲鎮瀾宮前的老街
tagline_en: Mazu, taro pastries and old bakeries around Zhenlan Temple
story_zh: 大甲老街以鎮瀾宮為中心，順天路、蔣公路一帶的老街屋大致勾勒出清代大甲城的輪廓。大甲媽祖每年遶境是台灣最大的宗教盛事之一，帶動了周邊糕餅、芋頭製品與藺草編織產業。附近的林氏貞孝坊是清代花崗石牌坊，為國定古蹟。
story_en: Dajia's old street radiates from Zhenlan Temple, and the shophouses along Shuntian and Jianggong roads still trace the outline of the old Qing-era town. The temple's annual Mazu pilgrimage is one of the largest religious processions in the world, and it sustains a cluster of bakeries, taro snack shops and the town's traditional rush-weaving trade. Nearby stands the granite Lin Family Chastity Arch from the Qing dynasty.
getting_there: 台鐵大甲站步行約8分鐘
best_time: 農曆三月大甲媽祖遶境起駕前後最熱鬧（也最擁擠）

address_hint: 文昌街、大街路一帶（紫雲巖周邊）
tagline_zh: 牛罵頭舊街，吃一碗清水米糕
tagline_en: The old 'Gumatou' quarter, home of Qingshui's famous sticky rice
story_zh: 清水舊名「牛罵頭」，1920年才因鰲峰山下的清泉改名「清水」。中山路開闢前，紫雲巖前的大街路是全鎮最繁華的街道，望族蔡源順家族與多家商號都在此開業。如今老街以住家為主，但周邊數十家米糕店仍是海線最有名的小吃之一。
story_en: Qingshui was called Gumatou until 1920, when it was renamed after a clear spring beneath Aofeng Hill. Before Zhongshan Road was cut through, the 'big street' in front of Ziyun Temple was the town's commercial heart, home to the wealthy Tsai family and their trading houses. Today the old streets are mostly residential, but the town's dozens of sticky-rice (migao) shops are a reason to stop.
getting_there: 台鐵清水站步行約10分鐘
best_time: 早上至中午米糕店營業時段

tagline_zh: 帆船港口留下的洗石子街屋
tagline_en: Granite-wash shophouses left by a vanished sailing port
story_zh: 梧棲古稱「五汊港」，道光年間開港後行棧林立，是中部帆船貿易的樞紐。今日所見街屋多是1935年關刀山大地震後重建，洗石子立面上仍刻著洪福泰、林吉安等商號名。隨著港口淤積南移、台中港新市區開發，老街逐漸冷清，只剩真武宮與日治警察派出所改建的文化出張所訴說往日風華。
story_en: Known as Wuchagang in the Qing, Wuqi became central Taiwan's junk-trade hub after its port opened in the Daoguang era, and the street filled with trading houses. Most facades you see today were rebuilt after the 1935 Hsinchu-Taichung earthquake, their granite-wash fronts still carved with merchant names. Silting and the later Taichung Harbor new town drained the street's life, leaving a quiet row of facades plus Zhenwu Temple and a restored Japanese police station.
getting_there: 台鐵沙鹿站或台中市區搭公車至梧棲，建議開車

address_hint: 四平街、中山路一帶（沙鹿市場周邊）
tagline_zh: 市場旁的舊街，生活味大於觀光
tagline_en: An everyday market street with little old architecture left
story_zh: 沙鹿舊稱「沙轆」，原是平埔拍瀑拉族沙轆社的所在地，清代漢人入墾後在此形成街市。四平街一帶靠近沙鹿市場與火車站，至今仍是日常採買的老商圈，但街屋多為戰後至1970年代建築，可看的老建築有限。
story_en: Shalu takes its name from Salach, a village of the Papora plains indigenous people, before Han settlers built a market town here in the Qing dynasty. The Siping Street area by the market and station is still a busy everyday shopping district, but nearly all the buildings are postwar, so there is little old architecture left to see.
getting_there: 台鐵沙鹿站步行約8分鐘

address_hint: 萬和路、南屯路口（萬和宮周邊）
tagline_zh: 台中最老的街：犁頭店與端午木屐競走
tagline_en: Taichung's oldest street, the 'Plough-shop Street'
story_zh: 南屯老街昔稱「犁頭店街」，清代因聚集製作、販售農具的打鐵店而得名，是台中盆地最早形成的街市之一。街頭的萬和宮創建於清雍正年間，為市定古蹟，街上仍有打鐵店、豆腐店、米麩店與中藥舖等老店。每年端午節的「穿木屐躦鯪鯉」競走是全台獨有的民俗活動。
story_en: Nantun was once called Litoudian, 'plough-shop street', after the blacksmiths who forged farm tools for the surrounding paddies, making it one of the earliest market streets in the Taichung basin. Wanhe Temple, founded in the Yongzheng era of the Qing, anchors the street, and a blacksmith, tofu maker, rice-flour shop and herbalists still trade along its 200 metres. Every Dragon Boat Festival locals race in wooden clogs in a custom found nowhere else in Taiwan.
getting_there: 台中市區搭公車至萬和宮站，或高鐵台中站開車約15分鐘
best_time: 端午節「穿木屐躦鯪鯉」活動最具特色

tagline_zh: 西大墩舊街，藏在商圈旁的百年土地公
tagline_en: The old Xidadun street and its 18th-century earth-god shrine
story_zh: 西屯老街原名「西大墩街」，是清代西大墩地區的街市，今日的光明路仍立有「西大墩街」石碑。街上的福德祠創立於1775年，與隆興宮、清靈宮同為清乾隆年間的地方信仰中心。老建築多已改建，如今是逢甲、西屯都會區中一條低調的生活老街。
story_en: Xitun Old Street was the Qing-era market of Xidadun, and a stone marker on Guangming Road still bears the old name. Its earth-god shrine dates to 1775 and, with two neighbouring temples, has served the area since the Qianlong era. The buildings have mostly been replaced, leaving a low-key neighbourhood street in the middle of booming western Taichung.
getting_there: 台中市區搭公車至西屯路站附近，步行可達

address_hint: 新興路一帶（福興宮周邊）
tagline_zh: 林爽文起事之地，河港「杙」字的由來
tagline_en: River landing where the Lin Shuangwen rebellion began
story_zh: 大里舊名「大里杙」，因大里溪水流湍急，商船須把竹筏繫在木樁（杙）上而得名，清代是大里溪畔的重要河港街市。街頭的福興宮創建早於1811年，被視為1786年林爽文事件的起義地，事件後清廷一度刻意壓制此地發展。老街如今相當安靜，留有大里杙文化館、鹹菜巷與一株倒栽榕。
story_en: Dali was originally Dalige, after the wooden stakes ('ge') to which boatmen tied their rafts against the fast current of the Dali River, and it thrived as a river-landing town in the Qing. Fuxing Temple at the head of the street predates 1811 and is remembered as the launch point of the 1786 Lin Shuangwen uprising, one of the largest revolts of Qing Taiwan. The street is quiet today, with a small culture museum, a pickled-mustard lane and an upside-down banyan.
getting_there: 台中市區搭公車至大里，建議開車或騎車

landmarks: 石岡車站舊址（東豐自行車道）
tagline_zh: 921震後重建的客家小街
tagline_en: A small Hakka street rebuilt after the 1999 quake
story_zh: 石岡是東勢線鐵路與東豐自行車道上的客家小鎮，老街屋在1999年921大地震中嚴重受損，多已重建。現在的老街以在地生活為主，較適合騎東豐綠廊時順道停留，搭配土牛客家文化館了解客庄歷史。
story_en: Shigang is a small Hakka town on the former Dongshi railway line, now the Dongfeng bike path. Its old shophouses were badly damaged in the 1999 Chi-Chi earthquake and most have been rebuilt, so the street is mainly local life today, best as a pause on the bike trail together with the Tuniu Hakka Cultural Hall.
getting_there: 台鐵豐原站轉公車至石岡，或沿東豐自行車道騎車

landmarks: 東勢客家文化園區（舊東勢車站）
tagline_zh: 大埔客語迴盪的宗教文化街
tagline_en: A Hakka old town where 'Dabu' Hakka is still spoken
story_zh: 東勢本街是東勢最早的街區，兩側新舊建築參半，街坊間仍能聽到少見的大埔腔客家話；約500公尺的街上就有七間廟宇，被稱為「宗教文化街」。東勢曾因大雪山林場與東勢線鐵路而繁榮，伐木結束、鐵路1991年停駛後，舊車站改為客家文化園區，與東豐自行車道相連。
story_en: Benjie, Dongshi's original street, mixes old and new buildings, and you can still hear the rare Dabu dialect of Hakka in its shops; seven temples line a 500-metre stretch, earning it the name 'street of religious culture'. The town boomed on timber from the Dasyueshan forests and the Dongshi railway branch; after logging ended and the line closed in 1991, the old station became a Hakka culture park at the end of the Dongfeng bike path.
getting_there: 台鐵豐原站轉公車至東勢，或沿東豐自行車道騎車

address_hint: 中和街一帶（區公所周邊）
tagline_zh: 花海與菇鄉之間的小街區
tagline_en: A small town street in the mushroom-and-flower highlands
story_zh: 新社以花海、香菇與果園聞名，聚落中心的老街區規模很小、資料也有限，舊建築多已改建。當地最具特色的民俗是無固定廟宇、由各庄輪流奉祀的「九庄媽」，每年農曆正月初遶境，號稱全台最早迎媽祖。
story_en: Xinshe is known for its flower fields, mushrooms and orchards; its small town-centre street is little documented and mostly rebuilt. The most distinctive local tradition is the 'Nine-Village Mazu', a goddess with no fixed temple who rotates between villages and is paraded in early January of the lunar year, said to be the first Mazu procession of the year in Taiwan.
getting_there: 建議開車
best_time: 農曆正月初三至初七九庄媽遶境
sources: https://www.culture.taichung.gov.tw/media/825896/巷內文化事-九庄媽-最平易近人的媽祖.pdf

tagline_zh: 車流中的舊街道，老屋多已不存
tagline_en: An old main road with little left of its past
story_zh: 神岡老街位於中山路一帶，是神岡庄舊時的商業街。如今是車流繁忙的地方幹道，兩側多為現代透天厝，可辨識的老建築不多；有興趣的旅人可轉往附近社口的林宅、筱雲山莊等清代宅第。
story_en: Shengang's old street was the commercial core of the former Shengang village along today's Zhongshan Road. It is now a busy local thoroughfare lined with modern townhouses and few recognisable old buildings; visitors interested in history are better served by the Qing-era mansions of nearby Shekou.
getting_there: 台鐵豐原站轉公車，建議開車

address_hint: 民族路與華山路口、開彰祖廟後方（新町溝沿岸）
tagline_zh: 古城護城河旁的日式散步道
tagline_en: A Japanese-flavoured stroll along Changhua's old moat
story_zh: 新町老街沿著「新町溝」而建，據考證這條水溝是彰化古城的護城河。溝旁仍留有部分日治時期的日式老屋與老樹，市公所整治後規劃為散步道，加上鳥居、石燈籠與涼亭等新設施。範圍不大，適合在彰化市區順道散步。
story_en: The 'Shinmachi' lane follows the Xinding ditch, believed to be part of the moat of Changhua's Qing-dynasty city wall. A few Japanese-era houses and old trees survive beside it, and the city has turned the bank into a short promenade with newly added torii, stone lanterns and a pavilion. It is small, an easy add-on while exploring Changhua city.
getting_there: 台鐵彰化站步行約15分鐘

tagline_zh: 一府二鹿三艋舺，台灣第一個古市街保存區
tagline_en: 'First Tainan, second Lukang': Taiwan's first protected historic street
story_zh: 鹿港是荷蘭及清代中台灣最重要的對外貿易港，留下「一府二鹿三艋舺」的說法。1934年市區改正拓寬了主街不見天，與之平行的瑤林街、埔頭街反而完整保留下長條形閩南紅磚店屋——前為店面、中為住家、後為院落，深達四、五十公尺以上。1986年這裡被劃為鹿港古市街保存區，是台灣第一個以整條市街為對象的保存案例，鎮上古蹟數量僅次於台南。
story_en: Lukang was central Taiwan's chief trading port under the Dutch and the Qing, remembered in the saying 'first Tainan, second Lukang, third Monga'. When the main covered street was widened in 1934, the parallel Yaolin and Putou streets escaped and kept their deep red-brick Minnan shophouses, with shop at the front, living quarters in the middle and courtyards behind, often 40 to 70 metres long. In 1986 they became Taiwan's first protected historic street district, and the town's tally of heritage sites is second only to Tainan.
getting_there: 台鐵／高鐵彰化站轉彰化客運至鹿港，車程約40分鐘
best_time: 平日上午較清幽；農曆三月媽祖誕辰與端午節慶最熱鬧

tagline_zh: 曾經「看不見天」的頂蓋商街
tagline_en: Once a roofed street where you could not see the sky
story_zh: 清代鹿港的主街「五福大街」在街道上方加蓋屋頂，行人不見天日、不怕風雨，因而被稱為「不見天街」，是當時最繁華的商業街。1934年日本當局實施市區改正，拆除頂蓋並拓寬為今日的中山路，兩側改建為日治時期的洋式立面街屋。現在中山路仍是鹿港主要的商店街，老餅舖、香鋪林立，只是當年的「不見天」已只能從老照片想像。
story_en: In the Qing dynasty Lukang's main street, Wufu Street, was roofed over so shoppers could walk without seeing the sky, earning it the name Bujiantian. In 1934 the Japanese authorities tore off the roof and widened it into today's Zhongshan Road, lined with Japanese-era Western-style facades. It is still Lukang's main shopping street, full of old bakeries and incense shops, but the covered street survives only in photographs.
getting_there: 台鐵／高鐵彰化站轉彰化客運至鹿港

address_hint: 員鹿路三段、太平街、彰水路三段一帶
tagline_zh: 庄役場古蹟旁的日治街屋群
tagline_en: Japanese-era shophouses around the old village office
story_zh: 溪湖老街又稱「溪湖中街」，以員鹿路三段為中心，路段上的溪湖庄役場是日治時期地方行政中心，已列為古蹟。太平街、彰水路一帶散布著老街屋，但曾經著名的東芳樓酒樓等建築已被拆除。溪湖另以羊肉爐與溪湖糖廠的五分車聞名，可一併安排。
story_en: Xihu's 'middle street' centres on Yuanlu Road section 3, where the Japanese-era Xihu village office survives as a heritage building. Scattered shophouses remain along Taiping and Zhangshui roads, though landmarks such as the Dongfang restaurant have been demolished. The town is better known for mutton hot pot and the sugar-cane train at the nearby Xihu sugar factory.
getting_there: 台鐵員林站轉公車至溪湖，建議開車

address_hint: 光文路、員集路三、四段（二水車站前）
tagline_zh: 車站前「三角仔」的三棟紅磚街屋
tagline_en: Three red-brick houses at the station-front 'triangle'
story_zh: 二水老街指二水車站前的光文路與相連的員集路一帶，是集集線支線的起點，昔日因鐵路轉運而繁榮。光文路與員集路交會的「三角仔」保留了三棟具特色的紅磚街屋：張老嚶宅、謝毛宅與鄭鼎宅（舊英源醫院）。街上以在地生活為主，適合搭集集線前後順道散步。
story_en: Ershui Old Street is the station-front strip of Guangwen and Yuanji roads; the town prospered as the junction where the Jiji branch line leaves the main line. At the 'triangle' where the two roads meet stand three distinctive red-brick houses, including the former Yingyuan clinic. It is a quiet local street, a pleasant stroll before or after riding the Jiji line.
getting_there: 台鐵二水站出站即達

landmarks: 竹塘火車站舊址（萬國煤氣行）
tagline_zh: 台糖五分車曾經駛過的小街
tagline_en: A village street where sugar trains once ran
story_zh: 竹塘老街位於中興街一帶，昔日台糖五分車田林線從街上經過，竹塘車站就在今日的萬國煤氣行前。糖業沒落後車站拆除、鐵道改鋪柏油，2019年台糖巡道車曾短暫重返老街引起話題。街上以民宅為主，可與附近的九龍大榕公、木棉花道串成鄉間小旅行。
story_en: Zhutang's old street, along today's Zhongxing Street, once had Taiwan Sugar's narrow-gauge cane railway running down it, with the village station where a gas-supply shop now stands. The station was demolished and the track paved over when the sugar industry declined, though an inspection railcar made a nostalgic return in 2019. It is a residential street, best combined with the village's giant banyan and kapok avenue.
getting_there: 建議開車
best_time: 3月木棉花季

address_hint: 光明街、中山路、中正路一帶（火車站前）
tagline_zh: 車站前的老商圈與肉圓
tagline_en: Station-front shopping lanes and Yuanlin's meatballs
story_zh: 員林舊市街位於火車站前，光明街一帶聚集服飾、鞋店與小店，中正路以小吃聞名，博愛路則是傳統市場的早市街。舊市街已高度發展，傳統街屋立面零星可見；最值得一試的是在地老字號的員林肉圓。
story_en: Yuanlin's old town is the grid in front of the railway station: Guangming Street is lined with clothing and shoe shops, Zhongzheng Road with snack stalls, and Bo'ai Road hosts the morning market. The district is densely redeveloped, with only scattered old facades, but the long-established local ba-wan (meatball) shops are reason enough to stop.
getting_there: 台鐵員林站出站步行約3分鐘
best_time: 傍晚光明街商圈最熱鬧

address_hint: 中正路、儒林路一帶（仁和宮周邊）
tagline_zh: 二林事件的發生地
tagline_en: Where Taiwan's first major farmers' protest began
story_zh: 二林是彰化西南部的老市街，仁和宮是當地最古老的媽祖廟，廟內保存清嘉慶年間的對聯與重修碑，列為縣定古蹟。1925年蔗農不滿製糖會社壓價而爆發的「二林事件」，是台灣農民運動的起點之一，仁和宮正是事件發生地之一。日治時期街肆繁榮、樓房林立，今日中正路一帶僅零星留有老街屋。
story_en: Erlin is an old market town in southwestern Changhua whose Renhe Temple, the area's oldest Mazu temple, preserves couplets and a stele from the Jiaqing era of the Qing. In 1925 cane farmers protesting low prices from the Japanese sugar company sparked the Erlin Incident, a milestone of Taiwan's farmers' movement, with the temple as one of its stages. The town prospered in the Japanese era, but only scattered old shophouses remain along Zhongzheng Road.
getting_there: 台鐵員林站轉公車至二林，建議開車

address_hint: 員集路、中洲路一帶（田中車站前）
tagline_zh: 大正紅磚與巴洛克立面並排的小鎮
tagline_en: A small town of Taishō red brick and baroque facades
story_zh: 田中老街位於田中火車站前的員集路、中洲路一帶，仍保存不少大正時期的紅磚街屋與昭和初期的巴洛克式街屋，例如約1930年由陳景崧醫師興建的景崧醫院。員集路過去是年節採買的熱鬧大街，如今已漸沒落，老布行等店家仍在營業，近年也有老屋改造的小店進駐。
story_en: Tianzhong's old street runs along Yuanji and Zhongzhou roads in front of the station, with a good number of Taishō-era red-brick shophouses and early-Shōwa baroque facades, including the Jingsong clinic built around 1930 by a local doctor. Yuanji Road was once the busy place to shop for New Year goods; it has quietened, though an old fabric shop still trades and some renovated houses now host small businesses.
getting_there: 台鐵田中站出站步行約3分鐘

address_hint: 斗苑路、中華路一帶（奠安宮周邊）
tagline_zh: 三角肉圓的故鄉，東螺溪畔舊河港
tagline_en: Home of the triangular ba-wan on an old river port
story_zh: 北斗古稱「寶斗」，清代是東螺溪畔的內陸河港，日治初期曾是南彰化第一大街庄。奠安宮前保存1857年的「嚴禁筏夫勒索示碑」，記錄當年過溪只能搭渡筏、常遭筏夫敲詐的往事。後來河床淤積、縱貫鐵路又未經過，北斗逐漸沒落，如今以手捏成三角元寶形的北斗肉圓最為人所知，奠安宮周邊有「肉圓一條街」。
story_en: Beidou, once called Baodou, was a Qing-era river port on the Dongluo River and in the early Japanese period the largest town in southern Changhua. A stele of 1857 in front of Dian'an Temple forbids ferrymen from extorting passengers, a reminder that crossing the river once meant relying on rafts. Silting and the main railway bypassing the town led to its decline; today it is famous for hand-shaped, triangular Beidou meatballs, with a whole row of ba-wan shops around the temple.
getting_there: 台鐵田中站或員林站轉公車至北斗，車程約20分鐘

address_hint: 永安街、永靖街一帶（永安宮周邊）
tagline_zh: 全台第一條私人集資建成的街
tagline_en: Said to be Taiwan's first privately funded town street
story_zh: 永靖街在清嘉慶年間由廣東饒平客家人倡議集資興建，被稱為全台第一條私人建街，後毀於道光六年閩粵械鬥，重建後以永安宮為中心發展。如今老戲院、旅社、雜貨店與理髮廳仍在，旁邊的永靖故事牆由在地畫家繪出五、六十年代街景。外地人以「永靖枝仔冰，冷冷硬硬」取笑當地獨特的「永靖腔」，是這裡有名的俚語。
story_en: Yongjing Street was laid out in the Jiaqing era by Hakka settlers from Raoping, Guangdong, who pooled their own money, and is often called Taiwan's first privately built street. It was destroyed in the 1826 Hokkien-Hakka feud and rebuilt around Yong'an Temple. An old cinema, inn, grocery and barbershop survive, and a mural wall by a local painter recreates the street in the 1950s and 60s. The famous jibe 'Yongjing ice pops, cold and hard' pokes fun at the locals' distinctive accent rather than any actual ice pop.
getting_there: 台鐵永靖站或員林站轉車，建議開車

address_hint: 中正路一帶（道東書院、和美市場周邊）
tagline_zh: 書院與紡織小鎮的舊街
tagline_en: Old town street of a Confucian academy and umbrella makers
story_zh: 和美的中正路是鎮上的舊商業街，附近的道東書院創建於1857年，是彰化縣保存最完整的清代書院，列為國定古蹟。往和美傳統市場方向走幾分鐘可抵日治時期的和美街長宿舍。和美曾以紡織與雨傘製造聞名，老街本身則以生活機能為主，老屋不多。
story_en: Zhongzheng Road was Hemei's commercial street; nearby Daodong Academy, founded in 1857, is the best-preserved Qing-dynasty academy in Changhua and a national monument. A few minutes past the market stands the Japanese-era residence of the town chief. Hemei was known for textile and umbrella workshops; the street itself is mostly everyday shops with few old buildings left.
getting_there: 台鐵彰化站轉公車至和美，車程約20分鐘

address_hint: 和平街（中正路至成功路之間）
tagline_zh: 草鞋墩的「新街」，近年已拓寬
tagline_en: Caotun's old 'new street', recently widened
story_zh: 草屯舊名「草鞋墩」，源於清代挑夫在此換草鞋休息。和平街相對於舊街被稱為「新街」，與中山街交叉口曾是輕便車的草屯站。街道長期狹窄成為交通瓶頸，近年已拓寬為12公尺道路，老街風貌大多不復存在。
story_en: Caotun's old name, Caoxiedun ('straw-sandal mound'), comes from porters who swapped worn sandals here in the Qing. Heping Street was the town's 'new street', with a push-car tramway stop where it met Zhongshan Street. Long a traffic bottleneck, it has recently been widened to 12 metres, and little of the old streetscape survives.
getting_there: 台中搭客運至草屯轉運站，步行約10分鐘

tagline_zh: 草鞋墩最早的街，舊屋多已改建
tagline_en: Caotun's first street, now largely rebuilt
story_zh: 玉峰街是草屯最早形成的「舊街」，清代為往來埔里與彰化的挑夫商旅歇腳之處。街上舊建築多已改建為現代樓房，可看的歷史痕跡有限，資料也不多。
story_en: Yufeng Street is Caotun's original 'old street', where porters and traders resting between Puli and Changhua gathered in the Qing dynasty. Most buildings have been rebuilt, there is little visible history left, and documentation is scarce.
getting_there: 台中搭客運至草屯轉運站，步行可達

address_hint: 廬山溫泉區（塔羅灣溪畔）
tagline_zh: 已公告廢止的溫泉街，店家多已撤離
tagline_en: A condemned hot-spring street, now mostly abandoned
story_zh: 廬山溫泉曾是中部最熱門的溫泉鄉，溪畔老街擠滿溫泉旅館與賣小米酒、山產的攤商。由於後方山體持續深層滑動、溪床淤積，南投縣政府於2012年公告廢止溫泉區，業者陸續遷往埔里福興農場的新園區，但拆遷與安置爭議至今未了。老街如今多數人去樓空，基於安全不建議前往。
story_en: Lushan was once central Taiwan's most popular hot-spring resort, its riverside street crowded with spa hotels and stalls selling millet wine and mountain produce. Because the mountain behind it is sliding and the river bed silting up, the county revoked the hot-spring zone in 2012 and businesses were told to relocate to a new site near Puli, though demolition and compensation disputes drag on. Most of the street is now deserted and visits are not recommended for safety reasons.
getting_there: 不建議前往
best_time: 颱風豪雨季節切勿前往

tagline_zh: 921後轉型的客家咖啡小街
tagline_en: A Hakka village street reinventing itself with coffee
story_zh: 國姓老街是鄉內最早開發的商店街，921大地震後多數商家外移到中興路，街區逐漸沒落。鄉公所推動老街再造，以國姓咖啡與客家美食為主題；國姓鄉如今是全台咖啡種植面積與產量最大的產區，也是第一個取得咖啡產地認證的鄉鎮。
story_en: Guoxing's old street was the township's first shopping street, but after the 1999 earthquake most businesses moved to Zhongxing Road and it declined. The township has tried to revive it around Hakka food and coffee: Guoxing now grows more coffee than anywhere else in Taiwan and was the first area to earn a coffee origin certification.
getting_there: 台中或埔里搭客運經國姓，建議開車

tagline_zh: 埔里打鐵街，手工刀具與農具
tagline_en: Puli's blacksmith street of hand-forged tools
story_zh: 埔里南興街舊稱「打鐵街」，過去聚集打鐵店，以手工打造刀具、鋤頭等農具供應盆地農家。隨著傳統產業式微，打鐵店已剩不多，街區以住宅為主；若遇到仍營業的師傅，可看到傳統鍛打工序。
story_en: Nanxing Street in Puli was known as Blacksmith Street, lined with forges making knives, hoes and other farm tools for the basin's farmers. With the decline of traditional trades only a few smithies remain among the houses; if one is open you can still watch hand forging.
getting_there: 台中搭客運至埔里轉運站，步行約15分鐘
best_time: 平日上午打鐵店較可能營業

tagline_zh: 集集線終點的木業小鎮
tagline_en: Timber town at the end of the Jiji line
story_zh: 車埕是集集線鐵路的終點站，日治時期為興建日月潭水力發電工程而設站，「車埕」意為「火車停放的空地」。戰後振昌木業在此設廠，木材集散讓小鎮盛極一時，1980年代禁伐後一度沒落。如今木業廠房改為展示館，搭配木造車站、儲木池與木桶便當，是集集線最上鏡的小站。
story_en: Checheng, 'the train yard', is the terminus of the Jiji branch line, built in the Japanese era to carry materials for the Sun Moon Lake hydroelectric project. After the war a timber company set up a mill here and the village boomed on logs until a logging ban in the 1980s. The mill is now a museum, and with its wooden station, log pond and wooden-bucket lunchboxes it is the most photogenic stop on the line.
getting_there: 台鐵集集線車埕站出站即達
best_time: 平日較清幽；搭集集線小火車前往最有氣氛

address_hint: 民生路、八張街一帶（集集車站周邊）
tagline_zh: 木造車站與綠色隧道，香蕉小鎮
tagline_en: Banana town with a wooden station and a tree tunnel
story_zh: 集集曾是清代通往水沙連的「集集街」，日治時期因集集線鐵路興建、運輸樟腦與木材、香蕉而繁榮。1999年921大地震震央就在附近，木造車站全毀後依原貌重建，武昌宮倒塌的廟身則被保留下來作為震災紀念。今日車站周邊老街以小吃與單車出租為主，搭配綠色隧道成為熱門小鎮旅行地。
story_en: Jiji was a Qing-era market on the route into the Shuishalian highlands and boomed in the Japanese era when the branch railway carried camphor, timber and bananas. The 1999 earthquake struck nearby, flattening the wooden station, which was rebuilt to its original design, while the collapsed Wuchang Temple was left as a memorial. Today the streets around the station are a family-friendly mix of snacks and bike rentals, close to the famous camphor-tree 'green tunnel'.
getting_there: 台鐵集集線集集站出站即達
best_time: 假日人潮多；可租單車騎綠色隧道

address_hint: 永平街一帶（鄉公所附近）
tagline_zh: 中寮山區的小村街，資料稀少
tagline_en: A tiny hill-village street with little documented
story_zh: 永平老街位於中寮鄉公所附近，曾有同名的永平戲院，是山區鄉鎮的生活中心。921地震時中寮受創極重，相關建築多已不存，目前能找到的歷史資料相當有限。
story_en: Yongping Old Street lies near the Zhongliao township office and once had a cinema of the same name, serving as the hill township's small centre. Zhongliao was among the hardest-hit areas in the 1999 earthquake, most old buildings are gone, and very little about the street is documented.
getting_there: 建議開車

address_hint: 下橫街、橫街一帶（連興宮周邊）
tagline_zh: 鄭氏部將林圯開墾的竹鄉老街
tagline_en: Bamboo town named after a Ming loyalist pioneer
story_zh: 竹山舊名「林圯埔」，得名於明鄭時期奉命前來開墾的部將林圯；日治時期約1920年因附近竹林茂密改名竹山。下橫街、橫街一帶是最早的街市，以清代創建的連興宮為信仰中心，廟口仍有肉圓、米糕等小吃。老街規模不大、特色店家有限，適合當作前往紫南宮、竹山文化園區時的順遊散步。
story_en: Zhushan was called Linqipu after Lin Qi, an officer of Koxinga's Ming-loyalist regime sent to open up the area; the Japanese renamed it 'Bamboo Mountain' around 1920 for the surrounding groves. The Xiahengjie and Hengjie lanes were the original market, centred on Lianxing Temple, where meatball and sticky-rice stalls still gather. The street is modest with few standout shops, best as a stroll combined with Zinan Temple or the Zhushan culture park.
getting_there: 高鐵雲林站或台鐵斗六站轉客運至竹山

landmarks: 太平老街巴洛克立面群
tagline_zh: 全台最長的巴洛克立面老街之一
tagline_en: One of Taiwan's longest rows of baroque facades
story_zh: 太平路在日治時期市區改正後重建，兩側街屋以大量巴洛克式山牆立面裝飾，商號名、家族堂號與花草浮雕排成約600公尺的連續街景，被認為是台灣保存最長的巴洛克老街之一。斗六當時是斗六廳的政經中心，富商競相在立面上展現財力。如今老街經整修後仍以在地商店為主，晚上點燈後更有味道。
story_en: Taiping Road was rebuilt during Japanese-era urban planning, and its shophouses were given ornate baroque gables decorated with merchant names, family hall names and floral reliefs, forming a continuous run of roughly 600 metres, often cited as one of the longest such streets in Taiwan. Douliu was then the seat of the regional government, and merchants competed to show off their wealth on their facades. Restored, it remains a working local shopping street and looks especially fine when lit at night.
getting_there: 台鐵斗六站步行約10分鐘
best_time: 傍晚至夜間點燈時段

image.commons_file: 斗六太平老街 Douliu Taiping Old Street - panoramio.jpg

tagline_zh: 醬油香飄的巴洛克老街
tagline_en: Baroque facades and the aroma of soy sauce
story_zh: 西螺位於濁水溪畔，清代以來是稻米集散的重要市街。延平路在日治時期市區改正後重建，兩側保留大量巴洛克、閩南與日式立面的街屋，是雲林最完整的老街之一。西螺的黑豆醬油遠近馳名，老街上可見醬油老舖，附近的西螺大橋曾是遠東第一長橋。
story_en: Xiluo sits on the banks of the Zhuoshui River and has been a rice-trading town since the Qing. Yanping Road was rebuilt in the Japanese era and retains a long stretch of baroque, Minnan and Japanese-style shopfronts, among the best preserved in Yunlin. The town is famous for black-bean soy sauce, with old breweries on the street, and the nearby Xiluo Bridge was once the longest in the Far East.
getting_there: 高鐵雲林站或台鐵斗六站轉客運至西螺

image.commons_file: 台灣省雲林縣西螺鎮延平老街.JPG

tagline_zh: 北港朝天宮前的百年香火大街
tagline_en: The pilgrimage street in front of Beigang's Mazu temple
story_zh: 北港古稱「笨港」，是清代台灣重要的河港，朝天宮創建於1700年，為台灣媽祖信仰的重鎮，每年農曆三月迎媽祖吸引大批香客。宮前中山路兩側是日治時期改建的立面街屋，聚集麻油、花生、糕餅老店與鴨肉飯等小吃，自古就是香客採買的大街。
story_en: Beigang, formerly Bengang, was an important river port in Qing Taiwan, and Chaotian Temple, founded in 1700, is one of the island's great Mazu shrines, drawing huge crowds of pilgrims for the goddess's festival in the third lunar month. Zhongshan Road in front of the temple is lined with Japanese-era facades housing sesame-oil mills, peanut-candy makers, bakeries and duck-rice stalls, a shopping street for pilgrims for centuries.
getting_there: 台鐵嘉義站或高鐵嘉義站轉客運至北港，車程約40分鐘
best_time: 農曆三月媽祖遶境期間最熱鬧（也最擁擠）

tagline_zh: 「北港顯，土庫定」的媽祖小鎮
tagline_en: A small Mazu town that stood beside mighty Beigang
story_zh: 土庫舊稱「塗褲」，信仰中心順天宮的媽祖被稱為「塗褲媽」，地方流傳「北港顯，土庫定」的說法。順天宮現今規模始建於1834年，日治後期因參與日本佛教宗派的開教計畫，迎請一尊觀音像，得以逃過寺廟整理運動的拆除。中正路兩旁仍有理髮店、相館、藥房與碾米廠等老店，可參加在地的街屋導覽。
story_en: Tuku, formerly Tuku 'mud trousers', venerates its Mazu at Shuntian Temple, and locals say 'Beigang's Mazu is famous, Tuku's is steady'. The current temple dates from 1834 and survived the late-colonial campaign to close temples by affiliating with a Japanese Buddhist sect and enshrining a Guanyin statue from Japan. Old barbers, photo studios, pharmacies and a rice mill still line Zhongzheng Road, and local groups run walking tours of the shophouses.
getting_there: 台鐵斗南站轉客運至土庫，建議開車

address_hint: 中山路、林森路一帶（糖廠周邊）
landmarks: 雲林布袋戲館（虎尾郡役所）
tagline_zh: 糖都與布袋戲的故鄉
tagline_en: Sugar capital and home of glove-puppet theatre
story_zh: 虎尾在1906年設立大日本製糖虎尾製糖所後迅速發展，曾是東洋第一大糖廠，因糖業繁盛有「小台北」之稱，至今仍是台灣少數持續製糖的廠區。直通糖廠的中山路一路是鎮上最熱鬧的街，沿線有虎尾郡役所（今雲林布袋戲館）、合同廳舍、虎尾驛等日治建築，近年老屋活化成咖啡店與書店。
story_en: Huwei grew rapidly after the Dai-Nippon Sugar company built its mill here in 1906, once the largest in East Asia, earning the town the nickname 'little Taipei'; it is still one of Taiwan's few working sugar mills. Zhongshan Road, which leads straight to the factory, has always been the town's busiest street and is lined with Japanese-era landmarks such as the former district office, now the Yunlin Glove Puppetry Museum, while renovated old houses host cafés and bookshops.
getting_there: 高鐵雲林站轉接駁車至虎尾，約15分鐘
best_time: 糖廠製糖期（約冬季至春季）可聞糖香

tagline_zh: 他里霧舊街與車站倉庫群
tagline_en: Old Talibu town and its station warehouses
story_zh: 斗南舊名「他里霧」，源自平埔族洪雅族的社名。1903年縱貫鐵路設站後，斗南成為雲林重要的農產轉運地，車站旁的舊倉庫群已活化為他里霧文化園區。中正路、中山路一帶的舊街以在地商業為主，零星留有日治時期街屋。
story_en: Dounan was originally Talibu, after a village of the Hoanya plains indigenous people. After the main railway arrived in 1903 the town became a key shipping point for Yunlin's farm produce, and the old warehouses beside the station have been turned into the Talibu culture park. The old streets along Zhongzheng and Zhongshan roads are mostly everyday shops with a few Japanese-era shophouses.
getting_there: 台鐵斗南站出站步行可達

tagline_zh: 海口的「台西第一街」
tagline_en: Taixi's 'First Street' on the oyster coast
story_zh: 台西舊稱「海口」，以養蚵、文蛤等養殖漁業聞名。中山路被稱為「台西第一街」，是當地最早開發的街道，日治至戰後初期為政商中心，部分建築仍留有巴洛克式雕飾。隨人口老化外移，許多老屋閒置，近年有團隊嘗試改造老屋。
story_en: Taixi, formerly called Haikou, is known for oyster and clam farming. Zhongshan Road, 'Taixi's First Street', was the area's earliest street and its commercial and political centre from the Japanese era into the early postwar years; a few buildings still carry baroque ornament. With an ageing, shrinking population many houses stand empty, though some have been renovated by local groups.
getting_there: 建議開車

address_hint: 中正路（東市場至西市場一帶）
tagline_zh: 本島人的「二通」，串起東西市場的嘉義老味道
tagline_en: Chiayi's "Second Avenue": old shops and market eats between East and West markets
story_zh: 日治時期嘉義的大通（今中山路）是官署與日人聚集處，外側的「二通」中正路則是本島人的生活商街，東市場與西市場都位在這條軸線上。街上至今仍有傳承數代的中藥房、針車行與老字號小吃，近年市府推動「二通老街社區活力計畫」與「二通圈生活節」，以導覽和老屋新業態重新喚回人潮。
story_en: Under Japanese rule Chiayi's main avenue (today Zhongshan Rd) was for officials and Japanese residents, while the parallel "Ertong" (Zhongzheng Rd) was the Taiwanese people's commercial street, anchored by the East and West markets. Multi-generation herb shops, sewing-machine dealers and old eateries still line it, and the city has revived it with guided walks and an annual Ertong neighbourhood festival.
getting_there: 嘉義火車站步行約15分鐘，或騎YouBike
best_time: 早上逛東市場最熱鬧

address_hint: 平和街、中山路一帶（大林車站周邊）
tagline_zh: 國際慢城裡的老旅社與老戲院散步
tagline_en: A Cittaslow town of old inns, a vintage cinema and quiet arcades
story_zh: 大林是台灣第一個獲國際慢城認證的城鎮，車站前的平和街一帶留有日治時期的街屋，例如前身為酒家、後轉做雜貨買賣的南榮行。在地團體以老旅社、老戲院串起散步路線，停業多年的萬國戲院也在進行修復活化。
story_en: Dalin was the first Taiwanese town certified as a Cittaslow. Around the station, Pinghe Street keeps Japanese-era shophouses, such as a former wine house later turned general store, and local groups run walking routes linking old inns and the long-shuttered Wanguo Theatre, now being restored.
getting_there: 台鐵大林車站出站即達
best_time: 平日慢慢逛，留意在地導覽活動

tagline_zh: 海拔千米的山產集散小街，順遊太平雲梯
tagline_en: A tiny mountain market street beside the Taiping Suspension Bridge
story_zh: 太平村位於梅山36彎之上，早年是山區茶葉、竹筍等山產的集散地，形成一條短短的老街。2017年太平雲梯開放後遊客大增，但不少人走完吊橋就離開，老街業者常說遊客「不知道有老街」。
story_en: Perched above Meishan's 36 hairpin bends, Taiping village grew as a collection point for mountain tea and bamboo shoots, leaving a short old street. Visitor numbers soared after the Taiping Suspension Bridge opened in 2017, yet many tourists cross the bridge and leave without discovering the street.
getting_there: 嘉義火車站搭公車至梅山，轉太平線公車；建議開車
best_time: 搭配太平雲梯，避開週三休館日；山路易暈車

tagline_zh: 阿里山鐵路中途站，便當飄香的山城老街
tagline_en: Mountain-rail halfway town famed for its railway bento
story_zh: 奮起湖海拔約1,400公尺，「湖」是台語的山坳，地名源自地形像畚箕。阿里山森林鐵路通車後，這裡成為上下山列車的中途補給站，乘客在月台買的便當讓「奮起湖便當」聲名遠播。車站旁沿階梯延伸的窄巷老街擠滿小吃與伴手禮，有「中台灣九份」之稱。
story_en: At about 1,400 m, Fenqihu's name ("dustpan hollow") describes its bowl-shaped valley—there is no lake. As the midway stop of the Alishan Forest Railway, it fed passengers boxed lunches on the platform, making the Fenqihu bento famous. The narrow stepped lanes beside the station, crammed with snack and souvenir stalls, have earned it the nickname "Jiufen of central Taiwan".
getting_there: 嘉義搭阿里山林鐵至奮起湖站，或搭台灣好行/嘉義縣公車
best_time: 平日上午人較少；週末易擁擠

tagline_zh: 從水庫底「扛」上來的竹管厝老街
tagline_en: A lakeside hamlet street of bamboo houses carried up from the reservoir bed
story_zh: 大埔是嘉義人口最少的鄉，曾有糖廠與戲院的繁華年代。1970年代興建曾文水庫時，村民把即將淹沒的竹管厝拆下、扛到高處重組，老街上僅存的幾座竹管厝就是這段「扛厝」記憶的見證。如今以筍乾、破布子和沙鍋魚頭聞名。
story_en: Dapu is Chiayi County's least populated township, once lively with a sugar mill and cinema. When the Zengwen Reservoir was built in the 1970s, villagers dismantled bamboo-frame houses from the valley floor and carried them uphill to rebuild; the few that survive on the old street recall that move. Today the area is known for dried bamboo shoots and fish-head casserole.
getting_there: 建議開車（台3線）
best_time: 搭配曾文水庫遊湖

address_hint: 中正路（和平街至忠孝街間）
tagline_zh: 時間凍結的鄉間商街，早市與百年藥房
tagline_en: A small-town street frozen in time, with a morning market and old herb shop
story_zh: 溪口舊名「雙溪口」，中正路老街約在清道光年間成市，1960年代全盛時藥房、銀樓、裁縫、相館、旅社與戲院林立。人口外移後商況冷清，卻也讓街屋保留了當年面貌；2012年鄉公所與藝術家合作的「秘密通道」裝置藝術為老街添了新趣味。
story_en: Formerly called Shuangxikou, Xikou's Zhongzheng Road became a market street around the 1830s and peaked in the 1960s with pharmacies, goldsmiths, tailors, photo studios, inns and a cinema. Depopulation left it quiet but largely unaltered, and a 2012 art-trail project added playful installations to its lanes.
getting_there: 台鐵大林站轉乘公車或騎車約15分鐘；建議開車
best_time: 早上忠孝街口早市最熱鬧

address_hint: 開元路、中正路、市東路一帶（配天宮周邊）
tagline_zh: 以配天宮為心，百年布行藥行與昭和洋樓
tagline_en: Old cloth shops, clinics and cinemas around Peitian Temple
story_zh: 朴子相傳因一棵朴樹下供奉媽祖而得名，配天宮（原名樸樹宮）是街區起源，周邊開元路的商業依廟而興。街上仍有近百年的布行、1921年創立的藥行，以及1930年代的日洋混合街屋清木屋、日新醫院和榮昌戲院。元宵節配天宮的「御賜燈花」是在地盛事。
story_en: Puzi grew around Peitian Temple, said to have begun as a Mazu shrine beneath a hackberry (pu) tree. Kaiyuan Road still has a near-century-old cloth shop, a pharmacy founded in 1921, and 1930s mixed-style buildings such as the Qingmu House café, Rixin Clinic and the shuttered Rongchang Theatre. Lantern Festival brings the temple's famous imperial lantern displays.
getting_there: 嘉義高鐵站或火車站搭嘉義縣公車至朴子
best_time: 元宵節配天宮燈花

tagline_zh: 「小上海」港鎮的舊街記憶
tagline_en: Faded memories of a harbour town once called "Little Shanghai"
story_zh: 布袋曾是鹽業與漁港重鎮，戰後一度有「小上海」之稱，市街以戲院與市場為核心。道路拓寬後舊街屋所剩無幾，如今遊客多直奔布袋漁港與觀光魚市，老街只剩地名與零星舊屋。
story_en: Budai was a hub of salt and fishing, nicknamed "Little Shanghai" in the post-war boom when its streets centred on a theatre and market. Road widening has removed most old shophouses; visitors now head straight to the harbour fish market, leaving the old street mostly a name.
getting_there: 嘉義火車站搭公車至布袋；建議開車
best_time: 順遊布袋漁港與高跟鞋教堂

tagline_zh: 台灣第一街，蜜餞蝦餅與劍獅的港口老街
tagline_en: "Taiwan's First Street": a port-town lane of candied fruit and sword lions
story_zh: 延平街是荷蘭人建熱蘭遮城時在城外形成的市街，被稱為「台灣第一街」。清代安平是府城外港，郊商雲集，各家門楣懸掛的「劍獅」用以避邪。2000年代延平街拓寬引發爭議，部分老屋遭拆，如今以蝦餅、蜜餞與小吃攤為主的觀光街，周邊巷弄仍藏著古厝與劍獅。
story_en: Yanping Street grew outside the Dutch Fort Zeelandia in the 1600s and is often called "Taiwan's first street". In the Qing era Anping was Tainan's outer port, and merchants mounted "sword lion" plaques over doorways to ward off evil. A controversial widening in the 2000s removed some old houses; today it is a busy strip of shrimp-cracker and candied-fruit shops, with older homes hidden in side alleys.
getting_there: 台南火車站搭2路、19路或台灣好行99號至安平古堡
best_time: 平日下午，傍晚可到安平港看夕陽

address_hint: 神農街（海安路至康樂街）
tagline_zh: 五條港的木造街屋，夜裡點亮燈籠
tagline_en: Lantern-lit wooden shophouses of the Five Canals port
story_zh: 神農街舊稱北勢街，位於五條港南勢港北岸，清代一樓是店面、二樓是倉庫，貨物直接從港道吊上樓。街尾的藥王廟奉祀神農大帝，金華府則是昔日碼頭工人的信仰中心。如今兩層木造街屋改成咖啡館、酒吧與藝廊，夜晚燈籠點亮最上相。
story_en: Shennong Street, once Beishi Street, ran along the north bank of one of Tainan's Five Canals; ground floors were shops and upper floors warehouses where goods were hoisted straight from the boats. The Medicine King Temple at its end honours Shennong, and Jinhua Temple served the dockworkers. Its two-storey wooden houses now hold cafés, bars and galleries, best seen lit by lanterns at night.
getting_there: 台南火車站搭公車至西門圓環/海安路，或騎YouBike
best_time: 傍晚至夜間，燈籠亮起時

tagline_zh: 珊瑚礁壓艙石堆成的府城渡口老街
tagline_en: A canal-port lane named after coral ballast stones
story_zh: 信義街位於五條港最北端的新港墘港，清代船隻從大陸返台時以珊瑚礁石（老古石）壓艙，卸下後堆在街邊，因此得名「老古石街」。街頭的兌悅門建於1835年，是府城大西門外城僅存的城門，至今仍可通行車輛，也因以老古石砌成而稱「老古石門」。
story_en: At the northern end of Tainan's Five Canals, ships returning from mainland China used coral rock as ballast and dumped it beside this street—hence the name "Old Coral Stone Street". Duiyue Gate, built in 1835 as part of the outer city wall, still stands at its head and is still used by traffic.
getting_there: 台南火車站騎YouBike約15分鐘；鄰近神農街
best_time: 可與神農街一起逛

address_hint: 新美街（成功路至民權路）
tagline_zh: 清代米商與紙莊雲集，府城父子進士的故鄉
tagline_en: Qing rice-merchant street with Tainan's famous father-son scholars
story_zh: 新美街北段清代稱「米街」，因米店林立而得名，1807年的《續修臺灣縣志》城池圖已有記載。附近還有許多紙莊與印製民俗版畫的店家；清代台灣唯一一對「父子進士」施瓊芳與施士潔也出身米街。今日街上散布老字號小吃與老屋小店。
story_en: The northern stretch of Xinmei Street was "Rice Street" in the Qing era, already marked on an 1807 county map, with paper shops and folk-print workshops nearby. It was home to Shi Qiongfang and Shi Shijie, Qing Taiwan's only father-and-son pair of imperial jinshi scholars. Today it mixes old snack shops with renovated houses.
getting_there: 台南火車站騎YouBike約10分鐘
best_time: 白天開店時段

tagline_zh: 五條港最早開發的河港街道
tagline_en: The oldest of the Five Canals harbour streets
story_zh: 南河街清初舊志多記為「南濠街」，是五條港中河道與街道並行的港道，也是最早開發的河港。從鎮渡頭沿今和平街向東可直抵城內大井頭，是出入大西門的要道。如今河道早已填平，只剩街名與零星老屋見證。
story_en: Recorded as Nanhao Street in early Qing gazetteers, this was the earliest-developed of the Five Canals, where canal and street ran side by side from the ferry landing to the Great Well inside the city. The canal is long filled in; only the alignment and a few old houses remain.
getting_there: 台南火車站騎YouBike約12分鐘
best_time: 可串連大井頭、神農街散步

tagline_zh: 府城巷弄裡的短短老巷
tagline_en: A short old lane hidden in central Tainan
story_zh: 北巷古街位於民生路一段132巷，是府城舊市區中保留舊巷弄紋理的一小段巷道，鄰近蝸牛巷、民生綠園一帶。公開資料極少，適合順路散步時留意，而非專程造訪。
story_en: This lane off Minsheng Road Sec. 1 keeps a fragment of old Tainan's alley pattern near Snail Alley and the old Minsheng roundabout. Very little documentation exists; treat it as a detour on a walk rather than a destination.
getting_there: 台南火車站騎YouBike約12分鐘

tagline_zh: 溪道上的連棟街屋與水流觀音
tagline_en: Row houses along a buried creek beside Qingshui Temple
story_zh: 開山路3巷原為枋溪河道，西側為六合境清水寺，因此舊稱「清水寺街」，又俗稱「水流觀音街」。巷內連棟街屋因未受道路拓寬影響而保持原貌，已登錄為歷史建築；2013年景觀改造時打開部分舊水道，重現枋溪意象。
story_en: This lane follows the old bed of the Fang Creek beside Qingshui Temple, earning the folk name "Floating Guanyin Street". Its row houses escaped road widening and are now a listed historic building; a 2013 redesign reopened part of the old watercourse to evoke the creek.
getting_there: 台南火車站騎YouBike約12分鐘
